title: Magnolia band in the Tenth of May parade
summary: The country band came to the city parade in white coats, played all day, and he talks about a musician who dropped dead and about Chris Kelly living nearby.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: What you did up here in the city?
And all the fellas used to give a layout every, around the 10th of May every year. Used to call it the 10th of May anyhow.
And they had our band came up. And we didn't even have uniform at that time. Well we got white coats, you know?

Just had a white coat and white cap. You could get a cap for 25 cents at that time, for that last year's day. Things was cheap. And my drum player, the bass drum player had to get a pair of tennis shoes like, you know? Black one, like that. His feet was hiding him and he had tennis shoes to make that parade. And then we went on that parade and all them bands, big bands, well we didn't think, we thought our band was the least on that, you know? And we went to playin' that day and they used to make some long parades. Just start around 8 o'clock, 9 o'clock and play until 5 and 6 o'clock in the evening. So we played and played. We'd see musicians got burnt out, you know? And setten out. That same son of Henry said, man, I'm gonna quit. I said, man, look at that man. One fella dropped dead, you see?
There was a fella who used to play, he's from this side too. He was playing with Allen, I think. He was playing with Allen's band. On that play?
Well, I guess maybe it might have been heart trouble or something else, you know? Someone like, when Walter Blue, when did he die?
Did you say Chris Kelly was with you at that time too? Was he playing with the Magnolia band?
No, no, no, no, no, no.
That was before he was right before his time?
No, he wasn't playing at all at that time, you see? By me being right there, he used to live just on this side of us, you see? He was about six miles above, but we know one another, you know?
Yeah, he doesn't belong to the Magnolia band.

No, no, he wasn't living right there on that plantation. He was living in a place where they arranged. Yeah. What they call it, they arranged now, that's where Chris was. And of course, he probably didn't have music on his mind at that time.
I interrupted you about your time about that parade though, that you played the 10th of May parade.

Yeah, we played and when we got, they said, we passed around and one of the ladies said, where did that fellas come from? Where's them white coats? You know when you passed, they did have different cracks, you see? Yeah. And they got on, got on time, they had a, what they call a district. That is where they got a... Yeah.
